TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Banda instrumented air range
DATE 20 May 2034 · 1000 local
SIDE USA
WINDOW 80 min, closes at 120
"Readiness is critical to an effective deterrence, not only in Air Force, but across all domains."
- Air Vice-Marshal Harvey Reynolds, Deputy Chief of Air Force, RAAF

BANDA INSTRUMENTED RANGE, 2034. This is the openly speculative test branch. Two identical US Navy F/A-18F aircraft carry SEST MALICE and SEST AIM-260 respectively; a third carries the AIM-174B Gunslinger interceptor fit. All start at the same altitude and speed, with weapons held. The target set contains a Felon, a J-20A, a J-15D and a KJ-500 at individually separated stations.

CLEAR disables target sensors. CONTESTED restores their normal sensor and electronic-warfare systems; nothing else in the scenario changes. Allow the engine to establish its tracks. Select one shooter, retain the others on Hold, and record the offered solution before closing the range. Repeat from a fresh start for the next weapon. The test is not deterministic: crew, detection, target manoeuvre and seeker behaviour can still vary.

The targets fly local loops with weapons held. The range ends when all four are destroyed. You can instead quit after recording a useful comparison. Use the same launch altitude, speed, target bearing and target state in both copies. Roosevelt is not deployed here; all blue aircraft recover to Langgur.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.
Wing Commander Daniel Ward; Range Controller Ellis
COMMANDER'S INTENT
Record offered launch range, actual firing range, target aspect, altitude and seeker outcome for each weapon. A kill is a test result, not proof of the range printed in the encyclopedia.
• Complete the four target engagements or exit after recording the comparison
• Preserve the three test aircraft
Three US Navy F/A-18Fs: four-MALICE fit, eight-JATM fit and Gunslinger interceptor fit. Langgur recovery field. Four target aircraft with weapons held: Su-57, J-20A, J-15D and KJ-500.

The planned window is 80 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 40 minutes more; the operation is closed at 120 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
